problem.text: The change combines cleanup with two behavioral edits: optional non-CUDA tensor inspection and explicit initialization of the quantizer's candidate minimum.

reasoning.text: A shared NUM_THREADS constant replaces three occurrences of 1024, keeping kernel iteration strides and launch sizing tied to the same value.

impact.text: list_gpu_tensors retains CUDA-only filtering by default; cuda_only=False permits other torch.Tensor devices through the existing size filter.

source_notes.text: The README edit only inserts “the” before “EXL3 format”; it does not revise or validate the surrounding performance claims.

limitations: No CUDA compilation, kernel execution, performance measurement or live tensor traversal was performed.
The scalar comparison check uses Python floating-point values, not CUDA float32 arithmetic; it establishes illustrative selection behavior rather than end-to-end quantizer correctness.

chapters.title: Quantizer cleanup and broader tensor diagnostics

claims.text: quantize_tiles_kernel processes 256-value tiles. For bit width K, its candidate loop examines 2^K states per outgoing edge, with 65536 >> K edges. The patch initializes min_err to INFINITY and min_in_edge to zero, then updates only on strictly smaller error, replacing unconditional acceptance of candidate zero.

For finite candidate errors, the strict comparison preserves the first minimum on ties. It is not universally equivalent for exceptional values: a scalar transcription selected the later finite value from [NaN, 2] under the new rule, whereas the old rule retained NaN.

NUM_THREADS remains 1024. A scalar enumeration verified complete, nonduplicated edge coverage for all dispatched K values 1–8: launches use 1024 threads for K=1–6, 512 for K=7 and 256 for K=8. This checks indexing, not GPU execution.

The diagnostic helper searches module globals and thread-frame locals, then follows object attributes, dictionary entries and sequence members. Its new comments explain this existing traversal; the functional extension is the optional device filter. Tensor sizes remain integer byte counts divided by 1024², so the documented megabytes are whole MiB, with a default minimum of one.

Collected records remain sorted by descending size and printed in per-device tables. The tabulate import moves from after traversal to the beginning of the helper, rather than becoming a module-level import or a newly declared dependency.

annotation.summary: Centralizes CUDA thread sizing, initializes candidate minima explicitly, and adds optional non-CUDA tensor listing alongside comments and a README wording correction.
